title: Trace Moisture Analyzer: 5 Proven Methods for Reliable Gas
text:
Analytical

 Trace Moisture Analyzer: 5 Proven Methods for Reliable Gas

 A few hundred parts per million of water can freeze a regulator, corrode a pipeline or lower the heating value of natural gas. Measuring that water quickly and correctly is the job of the analyzer and, just as much, of its sample system.

 
 ppmv and lb/MMscf 
 Aluminium Oxide 
 Quartz Crystal 
 TDLAS 
 Chilled Mirror 
 




 Water is the impurity every gas processor fights, from dehydration units to custody transfer points. This guide explains the units, the five main sensing methods, sample system rules and a quick lb/MMscf to ppmv calculator.


 
 Hello everyone, today we are going to learn how a trace moisture analyzer measures ppmv water in natural gas and process gases, which sensing methods are used, and how to design and maintain its sample system.


 
 
 
 What Is a Trace Moisture Analyzer?


 A trace moisture analyzer is an online or portable instrument that measures very small amounts of water vapour in a gas, usually in parts per million by volume (ppmv), lb/MMscf or dew point. It is one of the most important gas analyzers in natural gas processing, transmission and industrial gas plants.


 Ordinary relative humidity sensors, described in capacitive RH sensors , work well in room air but lose resolution in very dry gas. Trace levels need sensors and sample systems designed for single or double digit ppmv values.


 
 
 Image credit: AMETEK Process Instruments . Image courtesy of AMETEK Process Instruments, shown here for educational reference. 
 

 Water enters natural gas at the well and is removed in glycol or molecular sieve dehydration units. The trace moisture analyzer at the outlet confirms that the gas is dry enough before it enters the pipeline or a custody transfer station.


 
 
 Advertisement 


 
 


 Why Water Matters in Natural Gas


 AMETEK Process Instruments explains that water lowers the heating value of natural gas and dissolves H2S and CO2 to form corrosive acids. Under certain pressure and temperature conditions, water and methane also form solid hydrates that can block lines and force costly shutdowns.


 Pipeline and Gas Journal reports that the common US tariff limit is 7 lb of water per MMscf. The same article gives a typical European limit as a dew point of minus 8 °C at 70 bar absolute, and notes that suppliers who exceed limits can be shut in.


 
 7 lb/MMscf Common US pipeline tariff limit 

 147 ppmv Same limit expressed by volume 

 minus 8 °C Typical European limit at 70 bar(a) 

 0 to 525 ppmv Typical US analyzer range, 0 to 25 lb 




 Do You Know?
 Joule Thomson cooling across a pressure regulator can drop the gas temperature sharply. Wet gas can then form ice or hydrates right inside the regulator, even when the pipeline itself is warm.



 Units Used for Trace Moisture


 A trace moisture analyzer can report water in several ways, and engineers must convert between them every day. Gas volumes in lb/MMscf relate to flow units explained in MMSCFD natural gas flow rate .


 
 
 Unit Meaning Typical User 

 ppmv Volume of water per million volumes of gas Analyzer output, labs 

 lb/MMscf Pounds of water per million standard cubic feet US pipelines, tariffs 

 mg/Sm³ Milligrams per standard cubic metre European and Indian contracts 

 Dew point at pressure Temperature where water condenses at line pressure Hydrate and condensation checks 

 



 The dew point depends on pressure, so a value without a stated pressure is incomplete. The same idea is explained for compressed air in dew point in instrument air .


 5 Proven Trace Moisture Analyzer Methods


 
 Aluminium Oxide
 Porous oxide layer changes capacitance as it adsorbs water.
 Best for: low cost online points and dehydration outlets
 Economical 

 Quartz Crystal Microbalance
 Coated crystal frequency drops as water is adsorbed.
 Best for: fast response at ppmv levels
 Sensitive 

 TDLAS
 Laser absorption at a water line, no contact with the gas stream.
 Best for: dirty or sour gas, minimal upkeep
 Non contact 

 Chilled Mirror
 Mirror is cooled until dew or frost forms on it.
 Best for: reference and lab checks
 Fundamental 

 Electrolytic P2O5
 Water absorbed in a film is electrolysed, current gives content.
 Best for: clean dry gases
 Absolute 




 Each trace moisture analyzer method has a place, and many plants combine an online analyzer with a portable chilled mirror or second technology for spot checks. The comparison below helps match the method to the service.


 
 
 Method Strength Watch Out For 

 Aluminium oxide Low cost, wide range Drift, periodic recalibration 

 QCM Fast, sensitive Contamination of the coating 

 TDLAS No field calibration claimed, fast Higher price, background gas effects 

 Chilled mirror Direct physical reading Hydrocarbon dew point interference 

 Electrolytic Absolute principle Damage from liquids and high water 

 



 Aluminium Oxide Sensors in Practice


 An aluminium oxide sensor is a tiny capacitor whose porous oxide dielectric adsorbs water in proportion to its partial pressure. The capacitance or impedance is converted to dew point using a factory calibration curve.


 The Panametrics HygroPro XP datasheet gives a standard calibration from plus 10 to minus 80 °C dew point, with accuracy of plus or minus 2 °C above minus 100 °C. It is loop powered at 12 to 28 V dc with a 4 to 20 mA HART output.


 The same datasheet recommends sensor recalibration every 6 to 12 months, depending on the application.


 Quick Tip
 Keep a calibrated spare probe for every critical aluminium oxide point. Swapping probes takes minutes and avoids running the dehydration unit blind during recalibration.
